Rachel Lynde has a sonsy, kindly, and matronly appearance.

_Sources: [v3 ch.Again P16](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0016)_

## Personality

A capable and farseeing woman, this individual manages her own affairs alongside those of others. She is a kind and generous person, though she possesses a critical, officious, and bossy nature that inclines her to interfere with people of all ages. Known for being outspoken and opinionated, she maintains a pessimistic view of human nature and strongly believes in foreordination. Her habits include keeping a sharp eye on everything that passes, gossiping, and offering unsolicited advice. Deeply committed to church affairs, she is an active worker in her religious community and a passionate political enthusiast. Additionally, she is skilled in sewing and dressmaking, though she harbors doubts about the propriety of fiction writing and higher education for women.

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde was brought up with ten children, losing two over the years, and married at eighteen after attending school with a red-haired girl. A long-standing resident of [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) who knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts, she lived alongside [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) as a neighbor for forty-five years without a single quarrel. When Marilla's brother [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) set out to adopt an orphan boy, Rachel visited [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to investigate and warned [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) against taking in an unknown child. She later met the adopted girl, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), but offended her with blunt comments about her red hair, prompting an explosive outburst that ended only after [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) dramatically apologized to win Rachel's forgiveness and friendship. Over the years, Rachel often advised [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) on raising [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), including letting the girl stay home from school after a harsh punishment, and she even stepped in to sew [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves for [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) when [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) struggled to shop for it. She celebrated Anne's academic triumphs and offered comfort when [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) passed away suddenly, while continuously tracking local town developments. Following the death of her own husband, [Thomas Lynde](../character/thomas-lynde.md), Rachel accepted Marilla's invitation to move into [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) so she could remain in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), which cleared the way for [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to leave her teaching post for college. Living at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), Rachel helped care for the twins, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) and [Dora](../character/dora.md), while managing household affairs alongside [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md). She welcomed [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) home during college breaks, remained a staple of community news and wedding preparations, and eventually attended [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) Blythe's marriage ceremony before traveling to [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) to share [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) dinner at their new home.

## Quotes

> "I just guess she has done well, and far be it from me to be backward in saying it. You’re a credit to your friends, Anne, that’s what, and we’re all proud of you."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P48](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0048)

> "Child, yes, I’m afraid of it. Look at his face. When you’ve seen that look as often as I have you’ll know what it means."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P7](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0007)

> "I saw Mr. Harrison chasing your Jersey out of his oats today when I was coming home from Carmody. I thought he looked pretty mad. Did he make much of a rumpus?"
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 I An Irate Neighbor P38](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0038)

> "And every one of them said they liked you splendid, Anne, except Anthony Pye. I must admit he didn’t. He said you ‘weren’t any good, just like all girl teachers.’ There’s the Pye leaven for you. But never mind."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P26](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0026)

> "Well, I wish you would. I guess we’ll have the supper in about a fortnight’s time. Uncle Abe Andrews is prophesying rain and storms for about that time; and that’s a pretty sure sign we’ll have fine weather."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P8](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0008)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--rachel-lynde.md)

Rachel Lynde initially clashed with [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) when her blunt remarks about Anne's looks provoked a fiery outburst from the young girl, though Anne's eventual apology put an end to their early hostility. Over time, Rachel became a sounding board for Anne's troubles and offered practical advice regarding her upbringing. Their connection eventually grew into a warm friendship, with Rachel showing affectionate neighborly concern for Anne's health.
